- We want to avoid a large upfront commit in Y1; can we spread the committed units across 18 months instead of 12?
- We still need meaningful unit-cost protection (a price hold) for the first 12 months.

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Quick readout of options we can offer and why they map to your goals: 

1) Smoothing commit: spread the total committed units over 18 months with monthly minimums (instead of a single annual prepay). This keeps your cash outflow flatter while guaranteeing capacity for Redwood scheduling and pricing predictability.

2) Price hold: we can guarantee current unit pricing for the first 12 months from renewal signature; beyond 12 months, pricing reverts to an indexed ladder with caps.

3) Credit overlay: convert existing credits into an overlay that offsets per-token overage charges first (expires after 12 months). Credits not used against overage will convert to invoice credits in month 13.

I attached a short "Credit Overlay" term sheet and an initial SOW draft for procurement to redline. High level ask: if Celerium will commit to +30% capacity over current baseline under the smoothing profile, we can extend a one-time 10% onboarding credit and a 7% committed-rate discount across months 1–12.

Next steps: please confirm if smoothing + overlay is acceptable and I’ll loop in finance for final numbers and DocuSign.

Regards,
